name: Subscription System
author: joeyoungblood

sections.description:
Subscription System is a comprehensive WordPress plugin that provides a complete user registration and login solution for your website. With easy-to-use shortcodes and a user-friendly admin interface, you can quickly set up subscription forms and manage user registrations.

Key Features:

  • User Registration Forms – Create beautiful registration forms with username, email, and password fields
  • User Login Forms – Provide secure login functionality for your users
  • Admin Dashboard – Comprehensive admin interface to manage settings and view statistics
  • Shortcode Support – Easy integration with [subscription_register] and [subscription_login] shortcodes
  • Security Features – Built-in nonce verification and input sanitization
  • Responsive Design – Mobile-friendly forms that work on all devices
  • Translation Ready – Full internationalization support
  • WordPress Standards – Follows WordPress coding standards and best practices

Available Shortcodes:

  • [subs_sys_register] – Displays a user registration form (recommended)

  • [subs_sys_login] – Displays a user login form (recommended)

  • [subscription_register] – Legacy shortcode (still supported)
  • [subscription_login] – Legacy shortcode (still supported)

Admin Features:

  • Enable/disable user registration
  • View user statistics
  • Quick access to WordPress user management
  • Comprehensive help documentation
  • System status monitoring

Developer Information

Plugin Structure:
* Follows WordPress Plugin Boilerplate standards
* Object-oriented programming approach
* Proper separation of admin and public functionality
* Internationalization support
* Security best practices

Hooks and Filters:
The plugin provides various hooks and filters for developers to extend functionality. Documentation for these will be expanded in future versions.

Support:
For support and feature requests, please visit our website at https://mediahubster.in/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the subscription-system folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. Go to ‘Subscription System’ in your admin menu to configure settings
  4. Use the shortcodes [subs_sys_register] and [subs_sys_login] in your pages or posts
sections.faq:
How do I display a registration form?

Simply add the shortcode [subs_sys_register] to any page or post where you want the registration form to appear. The legacy shortcode [subscription_register] is also supported.

How do I display a login form?

Use the shortcode [subs_sys_login] in any page or post to display the login form. The legacy shortcode [subscription_login] is also supported.

Can I disable user registration?

Yes, go to the Subscription System settings page in your WordPress admin and toggle the “Enable User Registration” option.

Is the plugin translation ready?

Yes, the plugin is fully translation ready and includes proper internationalization support.

What happens after a user registers?

After successful registration, users can optionally be automatically logged in (depending on your settings) and will receive appropriate success messages.

Are the forms secure?

Yes, all forms include proper nonce verification, input sanitization, and follow WordPress security best practices.

1.0.22

Maintenance release — admin fixes, checkout stability, and feature toggles
* FIX: Subscribers admin page stylesheet now loads correctly (fixed screen ID mismatch that caused overlapping layout).
* FIX: Login, register, account, and checkout redirect URLs now respect custom Pages Settings instead of always sending visitors to wp-login.php.
* FIX: Stale Stripe customer IDs no longer crash checkout when a stored customer was deleted or belongs to a different Stripe mode.
* FIX: Content notification popup buttons (“Subscribe” / “Remind me later”) now work reliably; consolidated into content-notification.js.
* FIX: Database updater self-heals missing columns on upgrade (Stripe mode stamping, plan-switch scheduling, content subscription payment fields).
* FIX: Plan category labels no longer render blank when only one of the category_name/name columns is populated.
* FIX: Featured plan badge no longer fails when plan index is stored as a float string.
* NEW: Features tab in Settings — enable or disable Subscription Plans and Content Subscriptions independently; admin menu shows only enabled features.
* NEW: Per-plan customizable button label (e.g. “Buy Now” instead of “Subscribe Now”).
* NEW: Improved front-end asset cache busting (file modification time appended to script/style version strings).
* IMPROVED: Admin menu reorganized into logical feature blocks (Plans, Content, shared settings).
* REMOVED: The “This content is for subscribers” paywall. Gated posts no longer show a teaser + subscribe prompt — full content is always rendered. Existing installs are cleaned up automatically on update (the paywall’s stored setting is deleted); plans, checkout, webhooks and all other subscription features are unaffected.

1.0.21

  • Version bump for deployment tracking.

1.1.0

Centralized plans, and the content paywall — a core rebuild
* NEW: Content actually gets locked now. A the_content-based paywall shows a teaser + subscribe prompt on gated posts and grants full access only once Stripe confirms payment — previously every “gated” post was fully readable by anyone.
* NEW: One “Plans” screen. Create a plan, then say what it unlocks — whole site, a specific post/page, a category/tag, or a post type — instead of choosing between three separate, incompatible systems.
* NEW: One Stripe Product/Price sync, one checkout entry point, and one webhook endpoint with an idempotency ledger, replacing four competing/incomplete webhook implementations and the per-checkout ad hoc Stripe Product creation.
* SECURITY: Removed the Stripe secret key from the browser-side checkout flow (it was previously used to call Stripe’s API directly from the page). Checkout now always goes through the server.
* SECURITY: Paid access on content-plan and interest-subscription purchases now requires a Stripe-verified payment, not a trusted URL parameter.
* SECURITY: Fixed missing/incorrect authorization on subscription self-service actions (pause/resume) and several admin AJAX handlers.
* FIX: Rewrote uninstall.php, which previously left almost the entire schema behind.
* FIX: A fatal error that crashed any front-end page once a real content plan existed (content_ids parsing).
* FIX: Ten admin methods and three AJAX handlers that were called but never defined.
* Added a new, additive database layer (ss_plans/ss_plan_prices/ss_entitlement_rules/ss_subscriptions/ss_entitlements/ss_orders/ss_webhook_events) with a one-time, non-destructive backfill from all existing data — no existing table, option, or subscriber row is modified or removed.
* Channels/Work Items/Work Logs (an unrelated staff activity-log feature) moved to their own “Site Work Log” menu.

1.0.20

  • Subscribe modal: added configurable re-show delay after close (minutes, days, weeks, months)
  • Subscribe modal: fixed responsive layout with scrollable content and always-visible footer buttons
  • Subscribe modal: removed post-close cooldown banners for a less intrusive experience

1.0.18

Subscribe Button & Modal — Category / Tag Interest Subscriptions
* Added new “Subscribe Button & Modal” admin settings tab with full trigger, display, and context configuration
* Floating subscribe button with configurable position (bottom-right, bottom-left, bottom-center)
* Auto-open modal on page load with configurable delay
* Shortcode [subscriptionsystem_subscribe] to place a subscribe button anywhere
* Context-aware modal: automatically detects and pre-selects the current post’s categories and tags
* Logged-in user experience: hides name/email fields, greets user by name, and auto-fills their details
* Guest (not-logged-in) modal now shows a “Log in / Not now” panel instead of the full form
* After login, modal automatically reopens on the same page via ?ss_subscribe=1 URL parameter
* Session parameter is silently removed from the URL via history.replaceState after modal opens

Content Plans (Subscribe to Updates)
* Modal now sources plans exclusively from Subscription → Content Plans instead of generic plans
* Strict plan filtering: only shows plans whose categories/tags exactly match the current post
* Each plan card now displays which categories or tags it covers (e.g. “Category: Technology”)
* Conflict prevention: categories and tags already assigned to one active plan are shown as disabled (greyed out with “Used by: [Plan Name]” badge) when creating/editing another plan
* Backend validation blocks saving a plan with duplicate categories/tags — clear error message lists every conflict
* Content Plans admin list now has a Stripe column showing connection status (Connected / Mock / None)
* “Sync with Stripe” link on each Content Plan — creates/updates Stripe Product and Price, saves IDs back to DB
* Free content plans skip Stripe price creation (product only)

Checkout & Payment
* Interest subscription checkout now creates a real Stripe Checkout Session and redirects users to Stripe’s hosted payment page
* Plan lookup fixed to read from subscription_content_plans (or falls back to subscription_plans for legacy records)
* Uses pre-synced stripe_price_id when available; falls back to inline price_data for unsynced plans
* New /?action=interest_checkout_success handler: verifies Stripe session, activates the subscription, and shows a styled success page
* Cancelled Stripe sessions return to the checkout info page with a clear “Payment was cancelled” notice
* Fallback info page (when Stripe is not configured) now shows an admin-only “Configure Stripe →” button

Subscriber Experience Improvements
* Modal categories/tags list filtered to show only terms assigned to the current post (not all site terms)
* Section labels update contextually: “Categories in this post” / “Tags in this post” vs. “Select Categories”
* All post-specific categories and tags are pre-checked by default
* Intro text adapts: “Subscribe to get notified when new content is published in these topics.”
* Empty categories or tags sections are hidden rather than showing a placeholder

Plan Management (Subscription Plans)
* Add/Edit plan forms include Status (Active/Inactive), Max Categories, and Max Tags fields
* Plans list table shows Interest Limits (“Cat: X, Tags: Y”) and Status badge
* Backend correctly saves features JSON with max_categories, max_tags, and status on both create and update
